inputs: terrain-v3.0 artifacts: identical halo processing, fixed bins and 60/120/240 m scales. Only the distance-to-index conversion and the weights differ from v3.

formula.distance: W1 = sum over bins of |CDF_earth - CDF_planet| * bin width, on normalised fixed-bin histograms, in the feature's units
formula.notice: C is a similarity index from 0 to 100. It is not a probability, a confidence level or a percentage of identity.

slope.definition: Slope from metric x/y gradients (numpy.gradient on the metric grid); invalid cells propagate through the stencil.

local_relief.definition: Maximum minus minimum elevation in a 1,000 m square neighbourhood.

roughness.definition: Standard deviation of elevation in a 300 m square neighbourhood.

relative_elevation.definition: Relief-preserving relative elevation z - median(z) over the core AOI. Absolute datums are never compared. A shape-normalised variant (divided by spread) is not used because it would discard relief.

scale_support.note: SRTMGL1 posts at ~30 m and the Jezero CTX DEM at 20 m, so 60 m is the finest scale analysed (at least 2x the native posting).

tau_provenance: Each tau equals the terrain-v3.0 distance scale for that feature, carried over unchanged. Those values were set in Phase 5 after the three original Earth sites were seen. They were frozen on 2026-11-14 before the Phase 7 held-out sites (Dallol, Craters of the Moon, Hanksville, Meteor Crater) were processed, and were not tuned to favour any site.
weight_provenance: Equal family weights (0.25). This is a neutral provisional choice so that no family dominates; v3 used 0.15/0.30/0.20/0.35.
redundancy_policy: One distribution per family. Percentile summaries (p50, p90) are shown for interpretation only and never scored, so overlapping statistics are not double-counted. Correlation between family scores is reported by the calibration run.
